title: Month-End Cost of Care for a Notice-Billed Month: Medical Assistance Close Standard
content:
This close standard of Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage fixes the figure the business office reaches when a month billed on the County Assistance Office notice is reviewed against its cost of care.

## 1. The month and the charge
The review covers the calendar month before the current month and the case's patient pay charge billed from the notice (charge basis "actual notice") for that service month. The actual charge for the month is the amount billed on that charge less the reductions already posted for that service month; where no such charge was billed, the reduction is zero.

## 2. Residents and months with no reduction
The review covers a resident who holds exactly one funds account under Resident Trust Fund Accounts and exactly one coverage episode under Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage, each counted in every status, and no bed-hold reservation under Bed-Hold and Leave Reservations that ended because the hospital discharged the resident elsewhere; for any other resident it posts no reduction, and the partial-month rule and the base rule on the month's cost of care apply. No reduction is posted for a month that carries a patient pay charge with charge basis "partial month" or a reduction with reason "cost-of-care cap" for that service month, in which the case closed on the resident's discharge or death, in which the resident's funds account records the resident's discharge or death as the start of conveyance, or in which the resident's Medicare coverage ended because the resident was discharged from the center, transferred to a hospital without returning or died.

## 3. When the month is priced day by day
The month is priced day by day where all of the following hold:
- the bed-hold days booked for the month all belong to one bed-hold reservation;
- no Medicare coverage of the resident in status coverage ended or closed has its last covered date after the month;
- where the resident's Medicare coverage ended inside the month with the latest Skilled Nursing Facility Advance Beneficiary Notice on it recording option 1 or option 2, or a coverage under appeal has its last covered date before the month's end, that reservation's last held day falls no later than that coverage's last covered date, and no day away with no bed held falls in the month;
- where a hospice election date on the case falls inside the month, that reservation's last held day falls before the election day, no Part A day is booked for the month on or after the election day, no day away with no bed held falls in the month, the first non-covered date on such an advance notice falls before the election day, and the day after such an under-appeal coverage's last covered date falls before the election day.

For any other month the cost of care is the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, rounded half up to the cent, the days in the center being the month's calendar days less the bed-hold days booked for it and less the days away with no bed held counted as in section 4, never fewer than zero.

## 4. Day-by-day pricing
The cost of care a priced month carries is every calendar day of the month priced at the Medicaid daily rate on the case, except that:
- the Part A days Medicare covers in full (days booked for the month in benefit days 1 through 20, less the days reversed from those bookings) and the days a lapsed physician certification leaves to the center (days reversed as uncertified days from the month's bookings) carry no cost;
- the days the resident was away with no bed held carry no cost — for every bed-hold reservation of the resident in status declined, from its leave start; in status released, from the day after its release; and in status expired, from the day after its last held day; each up to the day before its return, or to the month's end where the resident has not come back, never fewer than zero in all;
- the Part A coinsurance days (days booked for the month in benefit days 21 through 100, less the days reversed from those bookings) are priced at the highest daily coinsurance booked for them.

The days at the Medicaid daily rate are the calendar days not taken out and not priced as coinsurance days, never fewer than zero. Each kind of day is priced and rounded half up to the cent, and the priced kinds are added to give the month's cost of care. Where two records share the latest date a reading goes by, the one posted first is read.

## 5. The reduction
The reduction is the actual charge for the month less that cost of care, never below zero, rounded half up to the cent, and it is posted against that charge with reason "cost-of-care cap".

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)
A 30-day month; Medicaid daily rate 274.63 dollars; notice charge 3,118.40 dollars with nothing yet reduced; the month is priced day by day; a skilled stay whose benefit days 1 through 20 fall on days 1 to 20 and whose benefit days 21 through 26 fall on days 21 to 26, booked at a daily coinsurance of 204.00 dollars, after which Part A coverage ended; nothing reversed, no days away.
- Days at the daily rate: 30 less 20 less 6, which is 4 days, costing 1,098.52 dollars.
- Coinsurance days: 6 days at 204.00 dollars, 1,224.00 dollars.
- Cost of care: 2,322.52 dollars.
- Reduction: 3,118.40 less 2,322.52, which is 795.88 dollars.

Had the same month failed the day-by-day test with 3 bed-hold days booked and no days away, its cost of care would be 27 days at 274.63 dollars, 7,415.01 dollars, above the charge, and the reduction would be zero.
